deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page is a draft for Riemann's 1851 Göttingen dissertation, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. The next page is the Vita and the letter to the Dean applying for the doctorate. The previous page drafts the conformal-mapping article (§20 in the draft; Art. 21 in print). The present page is a set of loose, heavily corrected fragments that were later redistributed over several articles of the printed text. No calculation is actually carried out on the page. Modern statements below are my reconstruction.

(a) Cross-cuts (cf. printed Art. 6). 'Letzteres kann auch in einem zur Begrenzung gehörenden Theile, also in einem äusseren Punkte des Querschnitts liegen.' The end point of a cross-cut (Querschnitt) may lie on a part already belonging to the boundary. That includes an earlier point of the same cross-cut, which after cutting has become boundary. This is the convention by which a cross-cut joins boundary to boundary and lowers the connectivity order by one.

(b) Integrals of exact differentials on the cut surface T* (cf. printed Arts. 9-10, and the ω-construction on the previous page). Let X dx + Y dy be a closed form on an n-fold connected surface T. Cut T by n-1 cross-cuts into the simply connected T*.
- The integral u(P) = ∫_{P0}^{P} (X dx + Y dy) is then single-valued and continuous on T*.
- Going across a cross-cut, u jumps by a constant along the whole cut. The reason: the two shores are traversed in opposite directions, and the integral around a small loop through the cut is path-independent.
- The sentence 'Wenn man den Querschnitt rückwärts ... durchläuft, so ist diese Bestimmung überall bestimmt, wenn der Werth im Beginn jedes Querschnitts gegeben wird; letztere Werthe aber sind von einander unabhängig' says the following. The determination is complete once the jump (value at the start) of each cross-cut is fixed, and these constants are mutually independent. In modern terms these are the periods (Periodicitätsmoduln) A_k = ∮_{γ_k} ω.

(c) Justifying the definition of 'function of z' (cf. printed Art. 1). 'Diese Voraussetzung ist in allen Fällen gerechtfertigt, wo sich auch dem Ausdrucke mittelst der Regeln der Differentiation ein Ausdruck von dw/dz finden lässt.' The assumption is that dw/dz is independent of the direction of dz, i.e. the Cauchy-Riemann equations u_x = v_y, u_y = -v_x. It is justified whenever w is given by an analytic expression in z that can be differentiated by the usual rules. This is nearly verbatim the printed justification.

(d) Dirichlet principle (cf. printed Arts. 16-18).
- Fragments: 'Wir verzichten darauf ...'; '... eine stetige Function ... einer unstetigen [beliebig] annähern kann, ohne dass L unendlich wird'; '... ein zusammenhängendes in sich abgeschlossenes Gebiet, indem eine jede dieser Functionen stetig in jede andere übergehen, sich aber [nicht] einer unstetigen unendlich annähern kann, ohne dass L unendlich wird.'
- Here L (Ω in print) is the Dirichlet-type integral ∫∫_T [(α_x - β_y)^2 + (α_y + β_x)^2] dx dy over the admissible functions λ.
- The printed sentence reads 'sich aber nicht einer längs einer Linie unstetigen unendlich annähern kann, ohne dass L unendlich wird'. The draft lacks the qualifier 'längs einer Linie'. The struck variants ('sich nicht beliebig', 'beliebig annehmbar') show Riemann struggling with exactly this point.
- The point is real: functions discontinuous at isolated points can be approximated with bounded Dirichlet integral. An example is log log(1/r), which has finite Dirichlet energy but is unbounded at 0. Line discontinuities cannot be approximated in this way.

(e) 'Die in den beiden vorigen Art. ausgesprochenen Principien' / 'Zur Veranschaulichung ... wird eine allgemeine Betrachtung über den Umfang der zur vollständigen Bestimmung einer solchen Function erforderlichen Bedingungen dienen.' This is the opening of the printed Art. 20, which counts the boundary and discontinuity conditions needed to determine a function.

(f) Marginal remark (bottom; very fragmentary).
- Gist: if at a single point of the surface (an isolated 'singulärer Begrenzungspunkt') a value is arbitrarily prescribed for a continuous function, this cannot enter the conditions 'für das Minimum von Ω'. At such a point one would need Ω' = 0.
- Consequently the boundary condition at such singular points has to be modified ('entsprechend f·Ω'').
- In modern language: a point has zero capacity. The infimum of the Dirichlet integral is unaffected by prescribing a value at an isolated point, so such a point condition cannot be imposed in the Dirichlet problem (cf. the Zaremba punctured-disk example). My reconstruction of this paragraph is tentative because of illegibility.
errors: No computational errors are possible since no calculation is carried out. However, the draft statement in (d) — that the admissible functions cannot approach a discontinuous one without L becoming infinite — is false as stated for point discontinuities. It is only true for discontinuities along a line. The printed version adds 'längs einer Linie', so Riemann corrected this himself.
The minimum principle itself (existence of a minimizer of Ω) is unjustified, as is well known (Weierstrass's 1870 criticism); this page only gestures at it.

results.what: On the cut surface T*, the integral of a closed differential is single-valued; it jumps by a constant across each cross-cut; the constants for different cuts are independent.
results.modern_name: Periods of closed differentials / homology basis of a multiply connected surface

results.what: Direction-independence of dw/dz is justified whenever w is an analytic expression in z.
results.usually_credited_to: Cauchy, d'Alembert, Euler; definition as foundation by Riemann 1851

results.what: The admissible functions form a connected, closed domain; they cannot approach a function discontinuous (along a line) with bounded L.
Prescribing a value of the function at an isolated point cannot affect the minimum of the Dirichlet integral; singular boundary points need a modified boundary condition.
results.modern_name: Zero capacity of points / irregular boundary points in the Dirichlet problem

results.what: Counting the conditions needed for complete determination of a function.
results.modern_name: Dimension counting for boundary-value problems (precursor to Riemann-Roch counting)

deep.surprise_reason: Almost all of the page is draft wording of known passages in the 1851 dissertation (Arts. 1, 6, 9-10, 17-18, 20). The only possibly non-standard item is the fragmentary marginal remark that a point value cannot enter the Dirichlet minimum; this foreshadows the zero capacity of points (Zaremba 1911). However, it is barely legible, and the printed 'längs einer Linie' already shows Riemann's awareness of the issue.

checkable.asserts: The Dirichlet energy of u=log(log(1/r)) on the disk r<1/e equals 2*pi, i.e. is finite. Here t=log(1/r), so 2*pi*Integral(1/(r*log(1/r)**2),(r,0,exp(-1))) reduces to 2*pi*Integral(1/t**2,(t,1,oo)). So a function unbounded at a point can have finite L.

Equals 0: the harmonic function equal to 1 on r=e and 0 on r=1 has Dirichlet integral 2*pi/log(1/e). This tends to 0 as e->0 (zero capacity of a point), so a value prescribed at a point does not affect the minimum.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',real=True); w=(x+I*y)**3; u=re(expand(w)); v=im(expand(w)); simplify(diff(u,x)-diff(v,y)), simplify(diff(u,y)+diff(v,x))
checkable.asserts: Both are 0: an analytic expression in z satisfies the Cauchy-Riemann equations, i.e. dw/dz is independent of direction.
The integral of d(arg z) = (x dy - y dx)/(x^2+y^2) around a loop crossing the cut of the annulus is 2*pi. This is the constant jump across the cross-cut (period).

transcription_corrections: Line 3 likely reads 'Wenn man den Querschnitt rückwärts (die zerstörten Theile) durchläuft, so ist diese Bestimmung überall bestimmt, wenn der Werth im Beginn jedes Querschnitts gegeben wird'.
The 'Diese Voraussetzung ...' sentence should end '... mittelst der Regeln der Differentiation ein Ausdruck von dw/dz finden lässt', not merely 'von z'. Compare the printed Art. 1.

In the Gebiet sentence, 'sich aber auch einem unstetigen' should very probably be 'sich aber nicht einer unstetigen unendlich annähern kann, ohne dass L unendlich wird'. This matches the printed text, minus 'längs einer Linie'.

'Zur Veranschaulichung' may be 'Zur Orientirung'. Compare the printed opening of Art. 20 ('eine allgemeine Betrachtung über den Umfang der zur vollständigen Bestimmung einer solchen Function erforderlichen Bedingungen').
The marginal note likely contains 'stetigen Function in einem einzelnen Punkte ein willkürlicher Werth beigelegt wird' and 'singulärer Begrenzungspunkt, wo Ω' = 0 sein müsste'.
